portInfo.description: Copenhagen Malmö Port (CMP) operates Visby’s cruise terminal on Gotland. CMP states nearly 170,000 cruise guests were expected in 2024 and that two 340-metre ships can berth at once. The dedicated cruises page lists pier LOA 360 m, 11 m water depth, 2.6 m quay height and max length 338 m, with commercial and operational contacts. Destination marketing (gotland.com) frames Visby as Scandinavia’s best-preserved medieval town with a UNESCO Hanseatic centre.

facts.established: Viking trading post, Hanseatic League member
facts.significance: Best preserved medieval city in Scandinavia

size.citySize: Main town of Gotland with population around 24,000

climate.description: Mild maritime climate with long summer days

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Visby cruise terminal / quay — Max length 338 m; dual 340 m capability claimed
gettingThere.walkingTime: 5-10 minutes to city center—confirm on your sailing programme before you rely on a fixed walk time.
gettingThere.publicTransport: CMP: terminal is within walking distance of the city centre. Exact minutes/path pins not verified — still keep a return buffer for wall-town crowds.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Medieval wall / inner town lanes — ~120 min.
Botanical gardens and church ruins — allow extra time; check hours locally.
Island countryside — coach; long call only.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Peak summer wall-town lanes congest — leave extra return time even though the walk is short.
